adversary.reason: [claude] The payer is verbatim H0007's registered payer — H0007's claim already reads 'Who pays: the liquidated leveraged long... the selling arrives in cascades' and already enumerated the cascade timescale (dip:0.10:7) — so 'this payer is different from every family already tested' is false against the registry; and the claimed novel shape is not novel: `orc/eval/simulate.py` has always held gated contributions as `powder` and deployed them when the gate opens, the identical code path H0007 ran, leaving `dip:0.08:1` as a third parameter pair on the same gate axis, i.e. a finer grid over an existing rule form (section 6). Compounding it, H0009 fixes include_funding=true and drops the with/without-funding control that is the exact clause H0007 closed on, so it cannot re-answer the question that killed its predecessor. | [codex] This is a finer-grid re-skin of closed H0007: it names the same liquidated-long payer and uses the same dip-gated cash-deployment rule, changing only the drawdown threshold and lookback from 10%/7 days and 20%/30 days to 8%/24 hours. The shorter lookback does not create a different rule shape, and an hourly trailing-peak gate still cannot identify or stand against the seconds-scale liquidation flow.

[codex] The claimed payer is not established: a mandate or margin rule normally constrains equity, leverage, or peak-to-trough loss, not pnl divided by cumulative contributions with permanent cessation of deposits. The proposal also misreads H0001’s drawdown-on-invested-capital metric: a 1344.9% peak-to-trough profit drawdown does not mean the account was thirteen times its contributed capital underwater.
